user_snapshot: Philosophy grad in Kano, fresh off NYSC, zero savings, zero income, living with parents. You have writing, research, and speaking — three tools that travel far in Nigeria if pointed at the right door.
headline_insight: Your ₦0 savings + ₦0 income + low risk tolerance means any route needing upfront cash (bootcamp, JAPA MSc, trade capital) is off the table in month one. But your writing/research/speaking skills can generate ₦50-150k within 60 days without spending a naira — and that's the unlock for everything else.

routes.title: Content & Copywriting → Remote USD Writer
routes.one_liner: Build a paid writing portfolio locally in 6 months, pivot to remote clients paying $500-2000/mo by month 12-18.

fit_reasons.note: Your Writing + Research skills are the literal job description — zero retraining cost.
₦0 savings works here; portfolio needs only data and laptop time, no fees.

break_reasons.risk: Kano location means low local agency density — you'll rely on LinkedIn/Twitter cold outreach, which punishes impatience

routes.who_this_fits: Writers who can publish 2 pieces weekly for 6 months with no applause and keep going.
routes.who_this_breaks: People who need external validation or a boss telling them what to write each day.

real_cost.what_you_give_up: Evenings and weekends for 12 months; social life shrinks while portfolio grows.

real_pay.range_note: Entry is local NGN gigs. Mid/senior pegged to USD ($500-$3000/mo at ₦1500/$).

routes.two_year_projection: In 2 years, if you publish weekly and pitch monthly, you're earning ₦600k-₦1.2m/mo from 2-3 retainer clients (US/UK SaaS blogs), working from Kano or relocated to Lagos, with ₦3m+ saved.
pro_tips: Publish on Medium + personal Substack — agencies Google your name before replying.
Pitch Nigerian fintechs (Paystack, Kuda) first — easier yes than cold US outreach.

monday_actions.step: Create Contra + Medium profiles, publish one 800-word piece on 'Philosophy applied to African business ethics' by Sunday

Join Superpath Slack and Nigerian Freelance Writers FB group; read 20 job posts to learn rate norms

routes.nigerian_notes: Kano's internet + power costs eat into remote work. Budget ₦25-40k/mo for data + small inverter by month 3. PalmPay/Grey for USD receivables.

routes.title: INGO Programs Officer (North-focused)
routes.one_liner: Enter humanitarian sector in Kano/Maiduguri — Philosophy + research + writing is a near-perfect fit, and the North is where INGOs hire.

fit_reasons.note: Kano is INGO-dense — Mercy Corps, IRC, MSF, UNICEF, NRC all have North-East/North-West ops hiring locally.
Writing + Research + Public speaking maps directly to reports, proposals, and community engagement roles.

break_reasons.risk: Entry NGO roles often require volunteer time first; 2-4 months of ₦0-₦50k stipend work to break in

routes.who_this_fits: Graduates comfortable writing donor reports, attending community meetings, and working in field conditions.
routes.who_this_breaks: Anyone expecting corporate pace or predictable 9-5; INGO work is deadline-chaotic.

real_cost.what_you_give_up: 2-4 months of volunteer/intern pay before full role; possible short deployments to Borno/Yobe.

real_pay.range_note: Local NGOs pay ₦80-150k entry. INGOs (UN, MSF, Mercy Corps) pay ₦250k+ with hazard allowance in conflict zones.

routes.two_year_projection: In 2 years, if you enter as program assistant at Mercy Corps Kano, you're a Programs Officer at ₦550-700k/mo, have led 2 donor proposals, and are eligible for UN roster roles.
pro_tips: Apply through ReliefWeb weekly — Nigerian INGO roles post there before local boards.
Volunteer 2 months at a local NGO for the reference letter — it unlocks INGO HR filters.

monday_actions.step: Create ReliefWeb profile, set email alerts for 'Kano', 'Nigeria', 'Programs', 'Communications'
Email 5 Kano-based INGOs (Mercy Corps, IRC, CRS, NRC, Save the Children) offering 2-month volunteer time
Write one 600-word LinkedIn post on a North Nigeria humanitarian issue using your Philosophy lens

routes.nigerian_notes: North-East INGO roles carry kidnapping/security risk — ask specifically about duty station before accepting. Hausa fluency is a massive hiring edge in Kano-based roles.

routes.title: Law Conversion (LL.B + Nigerian Law School)
routes.one_liner: Convert Philosophy into a 3-year direct-entry LL.B at ABU/BUK, then Law School — a slow but high-ceiling route.

fit_reasons.note: Your Writing + Research + Public speaking are the three core tools of legal practice — no wasted foundation.
BUK and ABU Zaria offer direct-entry LL.B close to home, avoiding relocation and Lagos rent.

break_reasons.risk: ₦0 savings + 4-5 year total timeline conflicts with medium family pressure and your 12-month horizon

routes.who_this_fits: Graduates with family able to fund ₦300-700k/yr for 4 years and who want courtroom or corporate law ceiling.
routes.who_this_breaks: Anyone who needs income within 2 years or whose family cannot sustain fees + upkeep for 4 years.

real_cost.what_you_give_up: 4-5 years of earning. Law School itself is ₦1m+. Need family or scholarship to fund.

real_pay.range_note: Entry at small firms ₦80-150k is brutal. Top commercial firms (Aluko & Oyebode, Banwo) pay ₦400-700k entry.

routes.two_year_projection: In 2 years, if you pass JUPEB/direct-entry, you're a 200-level LL.B student at BUK, earning ₦0 but with part-time writing retainer of ₦80-150k/mo keeping you afloat.
pro_tips: Target ABU Zaria direct entry — cheaper fees and strong Northern Bar network.
Apply for MacArthur or TETFund scholarships in year 1 — many Philosophy-to-Law converts win them.

monday_actions.step: Download JAMB direct-entry brochure, confirm ABU/BUK LL.B cutoffs and fees for 2025 cycle
Meet 2 practising lawyers in Kano (via parents' network or local NBA branch) to ask about funding + 4-year reality
Start running a paid writing side-hustle in parallel so this route doesn't depend on family alone

routes.nigerian_notes: Northern Nigerian LL.B programs are cheaper but Sharia-law heavy in electives — fine for most careers, matters only if you target specific commercial firms in Lagos. Call-to-Bar ceremony is ₦300k+ on its own.

routes.title: EdTech Content Producer / Instructional Writer
routes.one_liner: Write and voice educational content for uLesson, PrepClass, FlexiSAF — remote-first, uses all three of your skills, ₦150-400k/mo within 6 months.

fit_reasons.note: Writing + Research + Public speaking is the exact stack for curriculum writing and video-script narration roles.
Low risk tolerance fits — these are salaried remote roles, not freelance gambling.

break_reasons.risk: EdTech funding has tightened 2024-2026; hiring is slower and employers prefer 1+ yr teaching/content experience

routes.who_this_fits: Graduates who can explain hard ideas simply and take direction from curriculum leads.
routes.who_this_breaks: People who hate rewriting the same lesson 5 times to fit a style guide.

real_cost.what_you_give_up: ~₦15k for a decent USB mic (needed for narration samples); 2-3 months of unpaid sample production.

real_pay.range_note: uLesson, FlexiSAF, Gradely pay ₦180-300k entry. Senior instructional designers at international EdTech (Andela-adjacent) hit ₦700k+.

routes.two_year_projection: In 2 years, if you land a uLesson or Gradely content role, you're a Senior Content Producer at ₦500-650k/mo, remote from Kano, with a showreel strong enough for Coursera/edX contracts.
pro_tips: Record 3 sample 5-minute lesson videos on JAMB/WAEC topics before applying.
Pitch FlexiSAF Abuja directly — they hire Northern grads and value Hausa-language content.

routes.nigerian_notes: Most EdTech content roles are Lagos/Abuja HQ but fully remote-friendly post-2021. uLesson and FlexiSAF specifically hire Northern content producers for Hausa-medium content — your Kano base is an edge, not a handicap.
